title: Planning roles and links to the principles
blurb: Say who prepares, contributes to and approves each plan, and describe how the plans practice supports the seven principles.
question: A project manager sets work package tolerances and the executive sets stage tolerances. Which principle does this layered planning most directly apply?

teach.body: Plans are prepared by the project manager and team managers, shaped by the senior user and senior supplier, approved by the executive and the board, and set within standards and limits from the business layer. Project assurance checks progress against the agreed tolerances, and project support helps assemble the plans. Plain English: one person writes the plan, but several roles make sure it is realistic, consistent and approved.

head: Role
Planning focus
rows: Plans consistent with the user view
Plans consistent with the supplier view
Prepares plans and WPDs; applies stages
Schedules each work package; team plans
teach.caption: Project tolerances are documented by the business layer in the project mandate, or confirmed to the board for inclusion in the project brief.

teach.body: The project manager decides how stages and delivery steps are applied, prepares the project plan, stage plans and work package descriptions, and instructs corrective action when work-package-level tolerances are forecast to be exceeded. The senior user and senior supplier commit their resources to planning and check the plans from their perspectives, while the executive approves them.

teach.caption: Assurance is the board's independent check; support is administrative help for the PM. They must be kept separate.

teach.body: The plans practice puts several principles into action. Planning stage by stage applies manage by stages. Tolerances at each plan level apply manage by exception. Starting from products applies focus on products. Aligning a plan's targets with the business case, and giving estimates the board can judge viability on, applies ensure continued business justification. Lessons improve estimates, and the level of planning detail is tailored.

head: Principle
Plans in action
rows: Targets aligned to business case; estimates
Plans name who does the work

teach.h: Worked scenario: Marrowby Hospital's records project
teach.body: At Marrowby Hospital, the trust's PMO supplies its planning standards. Project manager Kemi Adeyemi prepares the stage 2 plan from the product descriptions and uses actual figures from a past records project to sharpen her estimates. Senior user Dr Alan Brook checks the plan leaves time for clinicians to test the system. Executive Ruth Okafor sets the stage tolerances and approves the plan. Project assurance later reviews progress against those tolerances.

teach.text: Setting tolerances is manage by exception, not manage by stages. Defining which products are in scope is focus on products, but the range allowed around that scope (scope tolerance) is manage by exception. And reviewing progress against tolerances is project assurance, not project support.

items: Business layer: planning standards and project tolerances (in the mandate or confirmed for the brief).
Executive: stage tolerances and approval of stage plans; senior user and senior supplier keep plans consistent with their views.
PM: prepares the project plan, stage plans and WPDs; decides how stages apply; corrects forecast WP breaches.
Team manager: schedules for each work package and team plans. Assurance reviews; support assists.
Plans apply manage by stages, manage by exception, focus on products and business justification, use lessons and are tailored.

summary: You can now say who prepares, contributes to and approves each plan, from the business layer's standards to the team manager's schedules. You can also link the plans practice to the principles, especially manage by stages, manage by exception and focus on products.

A.q: Which role provides the planning standards required by the business?
A.why: The business layer provides the planning standards required by the business (tab 7.1).

whyNot.0: The executive defines stage tolerances and approves plans; standards come from the business layer.
whyNot.2: Project support helps compile plans and maintains planning tools within the standards set.
whyNot.3: The project manager prepares plans using the standards the business provides.

A.q: Which role defines the tolerances for each stage and approves stage plans?
A.why: The executive defines tolerances for each stage and approves stage plans (tab 7.1).

whyNot.0: The senior user keeps plans consistent with the user perspective.
whyNot.1: The project manager prepares stage plans and sets work package tolerances.
whyNot.2: Project assurance reviews progress against agreed tolerances.

A.q: Which principle does product-based planning most directly support?
A.why: Product-based planning applies the focus on products principle (tab 7.2).

whyNot.0: Manage by stages is supported by the project plan and stage plans.
whyNot.1: Learn from experience is supported by using lessons in estimating.
whyNot.3: Manage by exception is supported by tolerances at each plan level.

B.q:
Which two statements about planning responsibilities are correct?
1. The senior user ensures plans remain consistent with the user perspective.
2. The team manager prepares schedules for each work package.
3. Project support reviews progress against the agreed tolerances.
4. The project manager sets the project tolerances.
B.why: The senior user keeps plans consistent with the user view, and team managers prepare work package schedules (tab 7.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: reviewing progress against tolerances is project assurance.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: the business layer sets project tolerances.
whyNot.3: Both are false: assurance reviews against tolerances, and the business layer sets project tolerances.

B.q: What is project assurance's focus in the plans practice?
options: Reviewing stage and project progress against tolerances
Preparing the work package descriptions with the team
Maintaining the planning tools and plan versions
Committing supplier resources to the planning work
B.why: Project assurance reviews stage and project progress against the agreed tolerances and advises on planning (tab 7.1).

whyNot.1: The project manager prepares work package descriptions, co-created with the team manager.
whyNot.2: Maintaining planning tools is project support's role.
whyNot.3: Committing supplier resources is the senior supplier's role.

B.q: A project manager aligns the plan's performance targets with the business case objectives and gives the board estimates to judge viability. Which principle is applied?
B.why: Aligning plan targets with business case objectives and providing estimates for viability decisions applies ensure continued business justification (7.7, tab 7.2).

whyNot.0: Focus on products is applied through product-based planning.
whyNot.1: Tailoring concerns the formality and detail of plans.
whyNot.2: Defining roles concerns who is accountable and responsible, not aligning targets with the business case.

C.q: A project manager uses actual durations from a similar past project to improve the plan. Which principle is applied, and in which planning step?
options: Focus on products; writing product descriptions
Manage by exception; preparing the budget
Manage by stages; organizing work packages
C.why: Using lessons from past projects in estimating applies learn from experience, in the preparing estimates step (7.3.1.3, tab 7.2).

whyNot.1: Product descriptions define the products; past durations are used for estimates.
whyNot.2: Manage by exception is applied through tolerances, and the budget is costed from the estimates.
whyNot.3: Organizing work packages groups the work; it is not where past durations improve the figures.

C.q: Who prepares the stage plans, and who approves them?
options: The team manager prepares them; the PM approves
The project manager prepares them; the executive approves
Project support prepares them; the senior user approves
The executive prepares them; the business layer approves
C.why: The project manager prepares stage plans; the executive approves them on behalf of the board (tab 7.1, 14.4.4).

whyNot.0: Team managers prepare team plans and work package schedules, not stage plans.
whyNot.2: Project support helps compile plans; the senior user checks the user view rather than approving.
whyNot.3: The executive approves stage plans; the business layer sets project tolerances.

C.q: Which is NOT a planning responsibility of the project manager?
options: Deciding how stages and delivery steps are applied
Setting the tolerances for the whole project
Instructing corrective action on forecast WP breaches
C.why: Project tolerances are set by the business layer, not the project manager (tab 7.1).

whyNot.0: Deciding how stages and delivery steps are applied is a PM responsibility.
whyNot.1: The PM prepares work package descriptions, co-created with the team manager.
whyNot.3: The PM instructs corrective action when work-package-level tolerances are forecast to be exceeded.

reteach.title: Who does what in a wedding plan
reteach.question: In a wedding, who sets the budget, who writes the plan, who checks it suits the guests, and who signs it off?

blocks.body: The family sets the overall budget and rules (business layer). The couple approves each phase (executive). The planner writes the plan (project manager). The caterer schedules the kitchen (team manager). A trusted friend checks things are on track (project assurance), and an assistant keeps the spreadsheets (project support).

blocks.text: Tolerances = manage by exception. Stage-by-stage planning = manage by stages. Product-based planning = focus on products.

explain.body: Provides the planning standards and sets the project tolerances, documenting them in the project mandate or confirming them to the board for the project brief.

test.q: Where does the business layer document project tolerances?
test.why: The business layer sets project tolerances and documents them in the project mandate, or confirms them to the board for the project brief (tab 7.1).

whyNot.1: The stage plan holds stage tolerances set by the board.
whyNot.2: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager in the work package description.
whyNot.3: The lessons log records lessons, not tolerances.

explain.body: Prepares the project plan, stage plans and WPDs, decides how stages and delivery steps are applied, and acts on forecast work package breaches.

test.q: Which role decides how stages and delivery steps are applied to the project?
test.why: The project manager decides how stages and delivery steps are applied (tab 7.1).

whyNot.0: The executive sets stage tolerances and approves stage plans.
whyNot.1: Team managers schedule their work packages and may produce team plans.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier keeps plans consistent with the supplier view and commits resources.

explain.body: Tolerances set at each level of plan let each level manage without referring up, unless a breach is forecast.

test.q: Setting tolerances at project, stage and work package level applies which principle?
test.why: Tolerances at each plan level apply manage by exception (tab 7.2).

whyNot.0: Manage by stages concerns planning and authorizing one stage at a time.
whyNot.2: Focus on products is applied through product-based planning.
whyNot.3: Learn from experience is applied by using lessons, for example in estimating.

explain.body: The formality and level of detail of plans are adjusted to suit the project: a small project may use simple plans, a large one more formal ones.

test.q: A small project uses short, informal stage plans while a large one uses detailed, formal plans. Which principle is shown?
test.why: Adjusting the formality and detail of plans to the project applies tailor to suit the project (tab 7.2).

whyNot.0: No roles or relationships are changing here.
whyNot.1: Business justification concerns whether the project remains worthwhile.
whyNot.3: Manage by exception is applied through tolerances, not plan formality.
